messages:
maria-finance: Heads up — bank reached out, chargeback from cardholder for acct_9081 (monthly infra). Claim: unauthorized, cross-border BIN (CA issuer) with 12 attempts in 2 hrs. They put a temporary hold on payouts. Need evidence packet and recommendation on representment by EOD.

sam-payments: Copy — can you drop the transaction ids and timeframe? I’ll pull auth logs and network traces.

maria-finance: Txns: TX-9271, TX-9272, TX-9275. Window: 2026-03-19 02:10–04:35 UTC. Amounts: $4,200 total. Customer email: ops+billing@acme-tools.com (logged).

ai-risk-bot: Automated alert: fraud_score=0.94, geo_velocity=HIGH, new_device_fingerprint=3/3 mismatches, recommended action = HOLD_ACCOUNT + EVIDENCE_SUBMIT.

leah-ops: Hold already placed on acct_9081 at 2026-03-19T05:12Z per policy. Customer notified with templated message (ref #billing-hold-template). I attached a copy of the email to the case.

frank-cs: Customer replied saying they didn’t authorize the charges and want a full refund immediately. They also asked if we can expedite — they escalated to their bank pre-dispute.

sam-payments: I pulled the following quick artifacts:
```
transactions.csv
mask_pan,txn_id,amount,country,auth_code
**** **** **** 4242,TX-9271,1200,US,AUTH42
**** **** **** 4243,TX-9272,1500,CA,AUTH43
**** **** **** 4244,TX-9275,1500,US,AUTH45
```
I’ll upload raw auth logs + acquirer response to S3 and share link.

maria-finance: Please include invoice PDFs, IP logs, device fingerprints, subscription activity (wasn’t a one-off charge technically). We need to know if this was abnormal usage or credential compromise.

sam-payments: Uploaded: https://internal-s3/redwood/chargebacks/1902345678/evidence.zip (restricted). Contains: invoices/, auth_logs/, ip_traces/, kyc_snapshot.pdf

ethan-legal: Quick note — redact full PAN and any unrelated PII before bundle sent to the issuing bank; we can include last4, masked PAN, and a short timeline. Also confirm we have customer IP consent in TOS for logs.

leah-ops: Redaction done on bundle. Also grabbed refund permissions for the account — acct owner is active and has signed agreement v2.1.

maria-finance: Observations from invoices: the subscription auto-renewed same day; usage history shows spike of long-running generation jobs between 02:05–03:00 UTC. Not typical for this account.

ai-risk-bot: Additional note: IPs associated appear to be from a VPN provider (ASN 63949) and two distinct geographic jumps within 30 min.

sam-payments: Given high fraud score + VPN + geo jumps, my recommendation is to contest representment but with caution — provide the evidence bundle and CVV/AVS data we have. If bank demands, we can provide device fingerprints.

frank-cs: Customer is pushing for refund; we can offer a partial goodwill credit while dispute resolves to keep them from escalating publicly. Need finance signoff.

maria-finance: Proposed plan: 1) Submit evidence packet to issuer (after redaction) to contest. 2) Offer temporary partial refund of $1,200 as goodwill pending outcome (notify risk/legal). 3) Keep payouts on hold. Approve? :thinking_face:

ethan-legal: OK to submit evidence. On the refund: prefer not to before representment result unless CS gets written confirmation they’ll withdraw dispute — risk of double-chargeback. Approve only if CS gets customer in writing.

leah-ops: I’ll ask CS to get written confirmation now. Also opening a ticket with acquirer operations for faster handling.

maria-finance: Sounds good. Sam — please kick off representment with the evidence link and tag me when submitted. Target: submit before 18:00 UTC.

sam-payments: Will submit and post confirmation here when done.

frank-cs: I’ll try to get the customer to send a short email confirming they’re willing to wait for review. If they agree to pause bank dispute we can consider the $1,200 credit.

ai-risk-bot: Incident summary appended to case #CB-2026-9081.

maria-finance: Thanks all — ping me for anything urgent. Will update thread after representment response.
